resources.title: International-school families cluster in Hellerup/Gentofte and Nordhavn
resources.body: For relocating families whose priority is English-language schooling, the practical anchor is school location: Rygaards International School and the International School of Hellerup sit in Hellerup/Gentofte, north of the centre, while Copenhagen International School (CIS) is in Nordhavn on the waterfront. Families commonly choose housing within reach of these areas. Central residential districts (e.g. Osterbro, Frederiksberg) are also popular but confirm commute and school catchment before signing.

resources.title: Driverless Metro + S-tog + buses, one check-in/out ticketing system
resources.body: Copenhagen has a fully automatic (driverless) Metro including the City Circle line and a branch to the airport (Kobenhavns Lufthavn), plus the S-tog suburban rail and buses. Ticketing across operators uses the Rejsekort (tap card / app): you MUST check in at the start of every journey, check in AGAIN whenever you change mode, and check out at the end — a missed check-in/out incurs penalties. The city is also heavily cycling-oriented.
resources.source_name: Rejsekort — How to travel (check in/out, official)

resources.title: Move-in cash: up to 6 months' rent up front
resources.body: Danish tenancy law lets a landlord require up to 3 months' rent as a deposit PLUS up to 3 months' prepaid rent — so a Copenhagen move-in can demand roughly six months' rent as an up-front lump sum (deposit is ring-fenced and refunded after an end-of-tenancy inspection; the prepaid rent covers the final months). This is a large, often-underestimated cash-flow hit at the start of a move.
resources.source_name: Aarhus University — Rent, deposit and contracts in Denmark

resources.title: English-language school capacity varies by grade — apply early
resources.body: Main English-language options are Copenhagen International School (CIS, IB, Nordhavn), Rygaards International School (Hellerup) and the International School of Hellerup. Availability is grade-specific and moves through the year: CIS, for example, publicly invites applications and reports spaces across grade levels for the 2026-27 year, but popular grades fill, so apply as early in the move as possible rather than assuming a place.

resources.title: CPR + MitID gate the bank account and public payments
resources.body: You need a CPR number to establish a NemKonto — the single account into which all Danish public payments (including tax refunds) are made — and MitID (the national eID, set up by scanning a passport chip in the app) to use online banking, public self-service and mandatory Digital Post. The working sequence is CPR -> MitID -> bank account -> NemKonto; nothing digital works before MitID is active.

resources.title: CPR delivers the yellow health card and an assigned GP
resources.body: Once registered with a CPR number you receive the yellow national health insurance card (sundhedskort) at your Danish address within about 2-3 weeks, showing your assigned family doctor (GP). GP care is free; hospital/specialist treatment normally requires a GP referral. Carry the yellow card for any doctor, dentist or hospital visit. No CPR = no GP and no card.
resources.source_name: Life in Denmark (borger.dk) — When you arrive (CPR, health card, GP)

resources.title: MitID and Digital Post run daily life; currency is DKK not euro
resources.body: Denmark is highly digital: MitID is every resident's key to public services and banking, and official communication arrives via mandatory Digital Post (e-Boks / mit.dk) rather than paper. The currency is the Danish krone (DKK), not the euro. Practically, an incoming employee cannot handle authority, tax or banking interactions until MitID is active, so treat it as a first-week priority.
